unresolved: north/south side of pike for 84th and 95th NY

notes: Verified: Cutler formed line with 76th NY, 147th NY, 56th PA; the 95th NY and 14th Brooklyn were detached to the left by Reynolds to support Hall's Second Maine Battery; Iron Brigade order 2nd, 7th WI, 19th IN, 24th MI with the 6th WI reserve. OPEN: which side of the pike. The row places the 84th/95th NY south of the pike; the OR says only "to the left" of Cutler and that Hall stood "on the right of the Cashtown road" (Hall p.359), which on its face is the north side facing west. The audit read it the same way. I do not resolve this from the OR; the position of the two regiments at first deployment needs the Bachelder/regimental sources. Flagged as conflict candidate, not a conflict finding. Row time window 10:00-10:30 agrees with Wadsworth ~10 a.m.

about noon arrived on the battle-field at Gettysburg

conflict_scenarios.value_a: fights with I Corps/Iron Brigade beside McPherson Woods 10:15-10:30
conflict_scenarios.source_b: OR vol.27 pt.1 R029 Doubleday p.255 + R067 Huidekoper p.346
conflict_scenarios.value_b: joins Wister's 150th PA (arrived ~noon), then the Iron Brigade after the retirement

notes: CORRECTS the T1 audit, which found no OR mention. Doubleday's report p.255 names "John Bums" (OCR for Burns; the OR index also lists "Burns, John. Mentioned 255"), a citizen of Gettysburg over seventy, who shouldered his musket and offered his services to Col. Wister, 150th Pennsylvania; he joined the skirmishers in the open fields, fought with the Iron Brigade when the troops retired, and was wounded in three places. CONFLICT with the row: row places him with the Iron Brigade beside McPherson Woods at 10:15-10:30; the OR ties him first to the 150th PA, which Huidekoper says arrived on the field about noon, so his fight cannot be at 10:15-10:30 on the OR account; the Iron Brigade association comes only after the troops retired. Existence and wounding are documented; time and unit are not as the row states. Carry both as scenarios.

supporting_passages.quote: A station of observation was established, first on the college

notes: Verified: a Union signal station of observation was set up on Jul 1 first on the college, then on the court-house (Norton). Jacobs 1864 (summarizer read, verbatim unverified, OCR "8J" read as 8 1/2): one of Howard's signal officers was on the College cupola about 8:30 a.m. and a College officer pointed him to Cemetery Hill; the text says "College cupola" and does not say Pennsylvania Hall in that reading. NOT verified: Prof. Jacobs being present with the officers on Jul 1 (consistent with his own narrative but unread here), and Confederate control of the cupola on the evening of Jul 1. Not an OR battle claim and the one source cited (HOSP-Aleteia, a Catholic news article) is secondary. A primary is needed: Surgeon Letterman's report and the Sisters of Charity accounts; neither was fetched in this shard. Tier documented is not earned here.
